content.text: Bonthron falsely implicates Rothsay, is hanged, secretly rescued by Dwining, Eviot, and Buncle, and taken by boat toward Newburgh. Rothsay is confined in Errol’s lodgings, then lured by Ramorny from Perth to Falkland, where he is imprisoned in a dungeon and starved. Catharine, held at Falkland, discovers him, feeds him through a wall, and sends Louise to seek Douglas; Douglas captures Falkland, but Rothsay is dead and Ramorny, Bonthron, and Dwining are executed. Simon Glover flees Perth to Loch Tay and seeks Clan Quhele’s protection. Eachin, secretly cowardly, loses the North Inch battle after Torquil and his foster brothers die; he escapes across the Tay and later leaps from Campsie’s cliffs. Henry Wynd fights for Clan Chattan, survives, marries Catharine, and becomes ancestor of respected families. The text then abruptly shifts to Descartes’s mechanistic philosophy, circulation of blood, animal bodies, reason, and the author’s reluctance to publish unfinished scientific work.
